meta.name: Windows Server Hybrid Administrator Associate (AZ-800)
meta.notes: Initial pack — 12 questions across the AZ-800 exam domains: Active Directory Domain Services, hybrid identity and management with Azure Arc and Windows Admin Center, Hyper-V and containers, on-premises and hybrid networking, and storage and file services. v1.1: +10 — RODC, GPO precedence, gMSA, SMB over QUIC, sites/subnets, Server Core management, Storage Replica async, DNS scavenging, hotpatch, shared-nothing live migration. [scheduled-agent hardening pass 2026-08-31: rebalanced answer positions (was A=12/22 with a run of 8 from q015–q022) to A=6/B=6/C=5/D=5 with no run > 2; rewrote self-contradictory load-balance/no-failover-relationship distractor on az800-007]

questions.question: After demoting the only domain controller that held the schema master and the domain naming master, your forest can no longer create new domains or extend the schema. You must transfer or seize these forest-wide roles to a surviving DC. Which two Flexible Single Master Operation (FSMO) roles are operating at the forest level?
options: PDC emulator and RID master
Infrastructure master and PDC emulator
Schema master and domain naming master
RID master and infrastructure master
questions.explanation: Active Directory defines five FSMO roles. The schema master and the domain naming master are forest-wide — only one of each exists in the entire forest. The PDC emulator, RID master, and infrastructure master are domain-wide and exist once per domain. The exam expects you to know which scope each role operates at and to use Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole (or, when the original holder is gone, seize the role with -Force).

questions.question: You need to project an on-premises Windows Server 2022 host into Azure so that you can apply Azure Policy, query it with Azure Resource Graph, run extensions such as the Log Analytics agent and Update Management, and target it from Microsoft Defender for Cloud — without migrating the workload to Azure. Which onboarding action should you perform on the server?
options: Install the Azure Virtual Machine Agent and register the server as an Azure VM
Install the Azure Connected Machine agent (azcmagent) and connect the server to Azure Arc
Add the server to a System Center Operations Manager management group and enable the Azure connector
Join the server to Microsoft Entra Domain Services and enable Microsoft Entra hybrid join
questions.explanation: Azure Arc-enabled servers project non-Azure machines into Azure as first-class resources. The Connected Machine agent (azcmagent) registers the server with Azure Resource Manager so Azure Policy, Resource Graph, Defender for Cloud, Update Management, and VM extensions can target it in place. The Azure VM Agent runs only inside Azure VMs. SCOM monitoring does not project the server as an ARM resource. Microsoft Entra hybrid join is a device-identity feature for Microsoft Entra ID and does not give the server an Azure resource ID.

questions.question: On a standalone Hyper-V host you want virtual machines to communicate with each other and with the host operating system, but those VMs must be completely isolated from the physical network. Which type of Hyper-V virtual switch should you create?
options: External virtual switch bound to a physical network adapter
External virtual switch with 'Allow management operating system to share this network adapter' cleared
Private virtual switch with no connection to the management OS
Internal virtual switch
questions.explanation: Hyper-V offers three virtual switch types. An internal switch connects VMs to each other and to the host (management OS) while remaining isolated from the physical network — exactly the requirement. A private switch connects VMs only to one another and excludes the host. An external switch is bound to a physical NIC, defeating the isolation requirement. Clearing the management OS sharing checkbox on an external switch only removes host connectivity; the VMs are still on the physical network.

questions.question: You need a single browser-based console to manage dozens of on-premises, Azure IaaS, and Azure Stack HCI Windows Servers — including Server Core hosts with no GUI — performing tasks such as role installation, registry editing, file transfer, and PowerShell remoting, with role-based access control and gateway-based deployment. Which Microsoft tool is purpose-built for this?
options: Windows Admin Center (WAC)
Server Manager from a Windows 11 Remote Server Administration Tools (RSAT) workstation
System Center Configuration Manager (now Microsoft Configuration Manager)
Microsoft Intune with the Windows Update for Business policies enabled
questions.explanation: Windows Admin Center is Microsoft's locally deployed, browser-based management tool for Windows Server, Azure Stack HCI, and Windows 10/11 clients. It is the recommended replacement for the classic in-box MMC consoles and works well with Server Core, supports gateway deployments, role-based access, Azure hybrid integrations (Backup, Arc, Update Management), PowerShell, files, and registry. RSAT/Server Manager is desktop-only and lacks the integrated browser experience and hybrid plug-ins. Configuration Manager is a heavyweight endpoint management platform for software distribution. Intune manages cloud-enrolled endpoints, not on-premises servers in this way.

questions.question: You are designing software-defined storage on four Windows Server Datacenter nodes equipped with local NVMe and SATA SSDs. The cluster must aggregate the local disks into a pooled, fault-tolerant volume that survives the loss of one or two nodes, with no shared SAN or external JBOD enclosure. Which feature should you deploy?
options: Storage Spaces with a single-server storage pool on each node
Cluster Shared Volumes on top of a shared iSCSI target served by one of the nodes
Storage Spaces Direct (S2D) on a Windows Server failover cluster
Distributed File System Namespaces (DFS-N) with replicated folder targets
questions.explanation: Storage Spaces Direct (S2D) is the Windows Server feature that pools each node's local DAS disks across a failover cluster into one fault-tolerant, software-defined storage system — no shared SAN or JBOD required. It supports mirror and parity resiliency that can tolerate node and disk failures and is the storage layer beneath Azure Stack HCI. Single-server Storage Spaces does not provide node-level resilience. Sharing an iSCSI target from one node creates a single point of failure. DFS Namespaces is a unified path overlay for file shares, not a block-level resilient storage layer.

questions.question: Your contoso.com DNS server must resolve names in the partner zone fabrikam.com by sending queries directly to fabrikam.com's listed authoritative name servers, while still resolving every other external name through the configured DNS forwarders. The fabrikam.com data must NOT be transferred to or stored locally. Which DNS configuration should you add on the contoso.com server?
options: A secondary copy of the fabrikam.com zone configured to perform regular zone transfers from the partner
A conditional forwarder for fabrikam.com pointing to the partner's name servers
A stub zone for fabrikam.com configured to refresh from the partner's authoritative name servers
A root hints entry referencing the partner's authoritative name servers
questions.explanation: A conditional forwarder routes queries for a specific DNS namespace (fabrikam.com) to designated servers; no zone data is stored locally and queries follow the normal recursive answer path. A secondary zone transfers and stores the entire zone. A stub zone stores the NS, SOA, and glue records and is refreshed from the master — it still stores data and is used to track which servers are authoritative, but the question asks for query forwarding with no local storage. Root hints describe the internet root servers and are not used for selective per-domain forwarding.

questions.question: Two DHCP servers must service the same IPv4 scope. If either server fails, the surviving server must be able to lease addresses from the entire address range without manual intervention, and the design should minimise the risk of duplicate leases. Which DHCP failover deployment mode best matches these requirements?
options: Two independent DHCP servers each holding 50 percent of the addresses, configured with the classic 80/20 split-scope rule
DHCP failover in load-balance mode where both servers actively answer requests from the same scope at a 50/50 ratio
Microsoft Failover Clustering hosting a single clustered DHCP role on a shared disk
DHCP failover in hot-standby mode between the two servers, with one server marked active and the other as a standby for the same scope
questions.explanation: Native DHCP failover (introduced in Windows Server 2012) offers two modes: load-balance, where both servers actively serve the same scope by a configured ratio, and hot-standby, where one server is active and the partner takes over after the maximum client lead time elapses. Both modes share scope state to prevent duplicate leases. The question specifies one active and one standby covering the full range, which is hot-standby. Split-scope (80/20) divides the pool so the standby can lease only a subset. Load-balance does not match the active/standby description. A clustered DHCP role is a legacy approach that requires shared storage and a single instance — not a failover pair.

questions.question: You must centrally deploy Windows Hello for Business in Hybrid Key Trust mode on a fleet of Microsoft Entra hybrid joined Windows 11 devices, configuring user enrollment, PIN complexity, and biometric gestures from a single management plane that flows down to domain-joined devices. Which Active Directory / Microsoft 365 capability should you use?
options: Group Policy Objects (GPOs) targeted at Computer and User configurations under Administrative Templates → Windows Components → Windows Hello for Business
Local Security Policy edits performed device-by-device with secpol.msc
PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC) pull server with a custom Hello configuration script
User Account Control (UAC) consent prompts configured through msconfig
questions.explanation: Windows Hello for Business is configured on hybrid joined devices through Group Policy under Computer/User Configuration → Administrative Templates → Windows Components → Windows Hello for Business (PIN complexity, biometrics, enrollment, security key sign-in). Intune configuration profiles are the equivalent for cloud-managed devices, but the question specifies hybrid joined domain devices managed centrally from AD. Local Security Policy must be repeated on every device. DSC is generic configuration management without Hello-specific templates. UAC governs elevation prompts and is unrelated to Hello enrollment.

questions.question: On a Windows Server container host you must run two containers side by side. Container A holds trusted internal code and may share the host kernel. Container B runs untrusted third-party code and must have stronger isolation, including its own kernel boundary, even though both images target the same Windows base image. What is the simplest way to achieve this?
options: Run both containers under default Windows Server isolation and disable network connectivity on container B
Run container A under default Windows Server isolation and start container B with the --isolation=hyperv flag (Hyper-V isolation)
Convert container B to a full virtual machine because Windows containers cannot provide kernel isolation
Apply a Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy that blocks system calls inside container B
questions.explanation: Windows containers support two isolation modes. Process (default) isolation shares the host kernel and is appropriate for trusted workloads. Hyper-V isolation runs each container inside its own lightweight Hyper-V utility VM with a dedicated kernel, providing strong isolation for untrusted code — selected per container by --isolation=hyperv. Disabling network on container B does not provide kernel isolation. Converting to a full VM is unnecessary and contradicts the requirement to use containers. WDAC is a code-integrity feature, not a container boundary.

questions.question: You must protect a 6 TB SQL Server LUN against the loss of the primary site by performing block-level, application-agnostic replication to a remote site at low latency. Replication must support synchronous mode so that an RPO of zero is achievable for short distances, and asynchronous mode for longer distances — all built into Windows Server without third-party software. Which feature should you use?
options: Distributed File System Replication (DFS-R) on the volume holding the database files
BranchCache configured in hosted-cache mode at the remote site
Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) Shadow Copies for Shared Folders scheduled every 15 minutes
Storage Replica configured for volume-level replication between the two servers or clusters
questions.explanation: Storage Replica is the in-box Windows Server feature that performs block-level, synchronous or asynchronous, volume-level replication between servers or stretch clusters — application-agnostic and certified for workloads like SQL Server. DFS-R is file-level, eventually consistent, and explicitly unsupported for open SQL Server database files. BranchCache caches HTTP/SMB content at branch offices for read acceleration, not site-to-site replication. VSS shadow copies are point-in-time local snapshots, not cross-site replication.

questions.question: You must synchronise identities from one Active Directory forest to Microsoft Entra ID. The deployment has fewer than 150,000 objects, requires lightweight agents on multiple servers for high availability, and does not need password hash sync customisations, full attribute filtering, or advanced features like device writeback and Microsoft Entra Domain Services support. Which synchronisation tool best matches these requirements?
options: Microsoft Identity Manager (MIM) 2016 with the Microsoft Entra ID connector
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync (formerly Azure AD Connect cloud sync)
Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) with the Web Application Proxy role
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync (formerly Azure AD Connect) running on a dedicated server
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync uses lightweight agents installed on multiple Windows servers (active/active), with sync orchestration in the cloud. It supports up to a few hundred thousand objects per scoping configuration and offers high-availability syncing with minimal on-premises footprint. Entra Connect Sync is the heavier on-premises engine required when you need advanced features like device writeback, full Exchange hybrid writeback, support for Microsoft Entra Domain Services, or large customisations — none of which are required here. MIM is a separate identity management product. AD FS provides federation, not directory synchronisation.

questions.question: Branch offices each host an SMB file server with 8 TB of frequently accessed shares. You must centralise the data in a single authoritative copy in the cloud, present an unchanged SMB experience to users, replicate changes from each branch to the central tier, and tier rarely accessed files off the local disk to free space while leaving stub files locally. Which Azure service should you deploy on each branch file server?
options: Azure Backup MARS agent backing up the volumes to a Recovery Services vault
Azure Site Recovery replicating each branch file server as a recovery VM in Azure
Azure NetApp Files volumes mounted to the branch file servers over the internet
Azure File Sync agent registered with an Azure Files share through a Storage Sync Service
questions.explanation: Azure File Sync turns Windows file servers into a hot cache of an Azure Files share. The agent registers each server to a Storage Sync Service, syncs changes bidirectionally, and uses cloud tiering to replace cold files with stub reparse points while keeping hot data local — preserving the existing SMB experience to clients. Azure Backup MARS only protects data; it does not present an SMB tier or do bi-directional sync. ASR replicates entire VMs for DR and does not provide a sync/cache topology. Azure NetApp Files is an Azure-hosted NFS/SMB service without a built-in branch caching agent.

questions.question: A branch office with weak physical security needs local authentication performance, but stolen hardware must not yield privileged credentials, and no changes may originate from that office's directory copy. Which AD DS role fits?
options: A writable domain controller in its own forest joined by a one-way external trust
A standalone member server running the LSASS caching service for branch logons
A read-only domain controller (RODC) with a password replication policy excluding privileged accounts
A global catalog server deployed in the branch with universal group membership caching disabled so lookups always traverse the WAN link
questions.explanation: RODCs hold a read-only copy of the database, accept no originating changes, and cache only the passwords its replication policy allows — privileged accounts excluded, so theft exposes nothing critical and delegated local admin doesn't grant domain rights. A separate forest is heavy machinery; there is no standalone 'LSASS caching service'; GC caching options affect logon lookups, not credential exposure.

questions.question: A computer object sits in OU Sales under OU Workstations in domain contoso.com, with GPOs linked at site, domain, and both OUs. Two GPOs set the same value differently. Absent enforcement or blocking, whose setting wins?
options: The site-linked GPO, because site-level links are always processed with the highest final priority in the chain
The GPO linked to the Sales OU — the closest link to the object is applied last and prevails
The domain-linked GPO, since domain scope always overrides organizational unit scope
Whichever GPO has the lower globally unique identifier when sorted alphabetically
questions.explanation: Processing order is Local → Site → Domain → OU (parent to child), and later application overwrites earlier conflicting values — so the GPO linked nearest the object (the Sales OU) wins by default. Enforced links and Block Inheritance alter this, which is exactly why the exam states their absence; GUIDs play no role.

questions.question: A Windows service across 30 servers runs under a shared domain account whose password hasn't changed in years. You want automatic password management, per-host constrained usage, and no password known to humans. What do you implement?
options: A group managed service account (gMSA), authorized for those 30 hosts, with the service configured to run under it
A new standard user account with a 64-character password stored in a sealed envelope
Local virtual accounts (NT SERVICE\name) on each server replacing the domain identity
A scheduled task that rotates the shared account's password every month and then updates the logon credentials on each of the thirty services in turn
questions.explanation: gMSAs have AD-managed 240-byte passwords rotated automatically every 30 days, retrievable only by the computers you authorize — no human ever knows the secret, and SPN/Kerberos handling is built in. Sealed envelopes and rotation scripts leave humans in the loop and break services on every rotation race; virtual accounts are local identities that can't authenticate as one principal across 30 machines.

questions.question: Remote workers need to reach on-premises SMB file shares from anywhere WITHOUT a VPN, over an encrypted, firewall-friendly transport on port 443. Which Windows Server 2022 capability provides this?
options: WebDAV publishing of every file share through an IIS reverse proxy with basic authentication
Opening TCP 445 inbound on the corporate firewall restricted to employees' home IP ranges
DirectAccess with the IP-HTTPS transition technology, deployed from a Windows Server 2012 R2 remote access template kept for compatibility
SMB over QUIC on Windows Server 2022 Azure Edition, tunnelling SMB 3.1.1 in TLS 1.3 over UDP 443
questions.explanation: SMB over QUIC wraps standard SMB in QUIC/TLS 1.3 on UDP 443 — 'SMB VPN-less', traversing firewalls like HTTPS with certificate-based encryption, an Azure Edition flagship feature. Exposing TCP 445 to the internet is the canonical anti-pattern; WebDAV changes the protocol and loses SMB semantics; DirectAccess is deprecated technology pre-dating the requirement.

questions.question: Users in the Madrid office intermittently authenticate against domain controllers in Sydney, causing slow logons. The DCs are healthy. What is the FIRST thing to verify in Active Directory?
options: That the PDC emulator FSMO role is held by a domain controller physically located in the Madrid office rather than in Sydney
That universal group membership caching is enabled on the Sydney domain controllers
That sites and subnet objects are defined correctly so Madrid's IP ranges map to the Madrid site
That SYSVOL replication has converged by forcing a non-authoritative DFSR restore
questions.explanation: DC locator steers clients to their own site's DCs — but only if subnet objects covering the client IP ranges are created and associated with the right site. Missing/wrong subnet mappings are the classic cause of cross-ocean authentication. PDC placement matters for password chaining, not locator behavior; UGMC and SYSVOL repair address different symptoms.

questions.question: You administer Server Core installations with no desktop experience. A colleague insists 'you cannot manage them without reinstalling the GUI'. Which combination is the actual management story?
options: Windows Admin Center, PowerShell remoting, RSAT tools from a workstation, and sconfig locally
Only the keyboard at the physical console, since Server Core blocks all remote management
Re-running setup to convert to Desktop Experience, which Windows Server 2022 supports in place
Installing a third-party window manager from the Microsoft Store on the Core host
questions.explanation: Server Core is managed remotely by design: WAC in the browser, PowerShell remoting/WinRM, RSAT MMC consoles targeting it from admin workstations, and sconfig for local basics. Remote management is on by default, the Desktop Experience cannot be added in place on 2016+ (reinstall required — the colleague has it backwards), and there is no Store window manager for Core.

questions.question: A two-site deployment needs volume replication for a file workload where the second site may lag slightly behind, since the WAN round-trip is 40 ms and write latency must stay low at the primary. Which Storage Replica mode is appropriate?
options: Synchronous replication, since it is the only mode Storage Replica supports across sites
Asynchronous replication — writes commit locally and replicate to the remote site shortly after
Hyper-V Replica with 30-second replication intervals applied directly to the file server's data volume through the replica broker
DFS Replication of the volume's block device through a staging folder on each member
questions.explanation: Storage Replica async mode acknowledges writes locally and ships log data to the partner continuously — built for higher-latency WANs where sync mode (which waits for the remote write, recommended ≤5 ms RTT) would throttle the application. Both modes exist; Hyper-V Replica replicates VMs, not arbitrary server volumes; DFSR replicates closed files, not blocks, and is unfit for open data sets.

questions.question: DNS zones are accumulating records for machines that no longer exist, breaking some name-based checks. What is the supported mechanism to remove stale records automatically?
options: Reducing every record's time-to-live to sixty seconds so that stale entries expire out of the zone file and resolver caches quickly
A nightly script deleting all records older than thirty days regardless of their owner
Switching the zone from Active Directory-integrated storage to a standard primary file
DNS aging and scavenging, configured on the zone and enabled on the server with appropriate refresh intervals
questions.explanation: Aging tracks each dynamically-registered record's last refresh timestamp; scavenging deletes records whose no-refresh + refresh windows have elapsed — the supported lifecycle for dynamic DNS hygiene. TTL governs cache lifetime, not zone contents; blanket deletion scripts kill static records and healthy hosts; zone storage type is orthogonal to staleness.

questions.question: Compliance demands security patches on a fleet of Windows Server 2022 Datacenter: Azure Edition VMs with the fewest possible reboots. Which capability directly reduces reboot frequency for monthly security updates?
options: Cluster-Aware Updating with a maintenance window defined for every fourth weekend
Delivery Optimization peering between the virtual machines so monthly updates download faster within each virtual network segment
Hotpatch, applying security updates to in-memory code with reboots only at periodic baselines
Switching the servers to the Long-Term Servicing Channel to receive fewer updates
questions.explanation: Hotpatch (an Azure Edition capability) patches running processes without restarting Windows for most months, requiring reboots only at quarterly baseline updates — directly cutting reboot count. CAU orchestrates reboots across a cluster but doesn't remove them; Delivery Optimization speeds downloads; servicing channels change feature cadence, not security-update reboots.

questions.question: You must live-migrate VMs between two standalone Hyper-V hosts (no cluster, no shared storage) in the same domain. Which feature and prerequisite make this possible?
options: Shared-nothing live migration, with constrained delegation (or CredSSP) configured for the hosts and migration networks enabled
Storage migration only — without a cluster, running VMs can never move between hosts
Quick migration, exporting the VM while suspended and importing it on the destination
Hyper-V Replica with planned failover and reversed replication, which transparently performs the equivalent of a live migration between the standalone hosts
questions.explanation: Shared-nothing live migration moves a running VM and its storage between standalone hosts over the network; it requires migration enabled on both hosts and authentication configured — Kerberos constrained delegation for remote management, or CredSSP with local sign-in. Clusters are not required; quick migration incurs downtime; Replica's planned failover is a brief outage failover, not live migration.
